comment: One row for each rule of part 1 of the leak rule of D17.20 in the emptiness pass
(src/fort/owner/prover.ft): the obligation of each exit kind, the scope of a named local at a
`return`, the facts and the bits that prove an exit, and the work limit. Then one row for each
rule of the error of the leak rule (src/fort/owner/report.ft), for the error in a build
(src/fort/gen_fir.ft) and under --check and --fir (src/fort/driver.ft), and for the option
--leak-report. The first stage runs the cases over FIR text and over lowered fort source
(test/fort/owner/prover_test.ft), with one case for each exit kind: the closing brace, `return`,
`break`, `continue` and an exit into an abort block, and the errors
(test/fort/owner/report_test.ft). The second runs the driver test, which holds the error in
each build mode, under --check and under --fir, and the empty list of --leak-report. The third
runs the oracle test, which prints a false accept for each row that makes the pass prove an exit
that a run leaks at. The fourth runs the fail tests of test/lang/fail/ownership, whose goldens
hold the error at each exit kind. The table runs in the Linux VM with the debug preset and the
default runner. The md5 guard reads the product compiler, whose driver and emitter import
The first round of a run can read stale (notes/testing.md 7), so the first row is one that

a store into a named local starts no scope
an address of a named local starts no scope
